svg.title: Finite Fourier coefficients and the fixed relative commutant
svg.desc: For a finite group acting outerly away from the identity on a II1 factor, finite matrix entries recover every crossed product coefficient. A faithful normal covariant realization has zero central kernel and a normal inverse. Applying it to the opposite factor gives Q prime equal to the fixed algebra N and N prime intersect M equal to the scalars. This is a proof dependency diagram, not a diagram of an infinite group construction.
svg.metadata: New original reproducible vector diagram, CC0. Proof locators: finite-outer-actions.html, equations (2)–(4), Lemmas 1.2–1.3, identities (FJ1)–(FJ3), Theorem 2.1. Human method: Jesse Peterson, Notes on operator algebras, April 27, 2020, Proposition 6.4.12, p.107, https://math.vanderbilt.edu/peters10/teaching/spring2020/OperatorAlgebras.pdf; Claire Anantharaman and Sorin Popa, An introduction to II1 factors, author draft, section 5.2 and Exercise 5.11, https://idpoisson.fr/anantharaman/publications/IIun.pdf.
svg.text: Finite coefficients → fixed commutant
G finite; M a II₁ factor; αg outer for g ≠ e.
1. Read each coefficient from one entry
P = M ⋊ G, X = Σg∈G π(xg)Ug
bt,s = αt⁻¹(xts⁻¹)
xg = be,g⁻¹, ‖xg‖ ≤ ‖X‖
Finite normal matrix slices; unique expansion.
Equations (2)–(4); Lemma 1.2 makes P a factor.
2. Realize the whole finite algebra
Φ(X) = Σg∈G ρ(xg)Vg
ker Φ = Pz, z central; unitality forces z = 0.
Normal isomorphism onto (ρ(M) ∪ V(G))″.
Lemma 1.3; ST1–2 proves the full normal inverse.
3. Apply this to the opposite factor
J(xΩ) = x*Ω, JMJ = M′
Identities (FJ1)–(FJ3), on the whole GNS space.
N = MG; hence Q = N′.
Theorem 2.1 · finite outer actions · proof diagram · CC0
